newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent lower.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.10 cent weaker Friday, based on market orders at 1018 EDT, traders said.
USDA's July estimates for the 1997/98 crop are expected to have very little effect on the market, analysts said.

USDA put the crop at 18.0 million 480-lb bales versus 18.5 million bales in its June report. Exports were seen at 7.1 million bales compared with 7.3 million bales, and ending stocks unchanged at 3.95 million bales.

Technically, the market may be positioned to move higher. Analyst Sharon Johnson of Frank Schneider and Co Inc said that while the market fell to new contract lows on Thursday, it settled above the closing price on Monday, when December hit its previous contract low.
"It's a bullish signal that prices went lower but closed higher (on Thursday versus Monday)," Johnson said.
The brisk trade buying that absorbed a gread deal of the selling on Thursday is expected to persist today, analysts said, pegging nearby resistance in December at 75.00 cents.
Thursday, the benchmark December contract closed down 0.32 cent at 74.03 cents a lb after ranging from 74.20 to 73.40 cents, a new contract low.
Support in December was put at 73.70 cents, followed by 72.00 cents.
